item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
366
ABPZ20 KNHC 060513
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
1100 PM PDT Mon Oct 5 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Hurricane
Rachel, located several hundred miles west-southwest of the
southern tip of the Baja California Peninsula.

South of Southern Mexico (92E):
A broad area of low pressure located offshore of southern Mexico is
producing disorganized showers and thunderstorms. Environmental
conditions appear favorable for gradual development, and a tropical
depression is likely to form within the next couple of days while
the system moves slowly west-northwestward to northwestward.
Interests along the coast of southwestern Mexico should monitor the
progress of this system.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...high...80 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

$$
Forecaster Gibbs

item.description: ...RACHEL WEAKENS SLIGHTLY WHILE CONTINUING WESTWARD... As of 2:00 AM PDT Tue Oct 06 the center of Rachel was located near 20.3, -118.6 with movement W at 8 mph. The minimum central pressure was 976 mb with maximum sustained winds of about 85 mph.

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Public Advisory Number 37
item.description:
Issued at 200 AM PDT Tue Oct 06 2026 
000
WTPZ33 KNHC 060839
TCPEP3
 
BULLETIN
Hurricane Rachel Advisory Number  37
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
200 AM PDT Tue Oct 06 2026
 
...RACHEL WEAKENS SLIGHTLY WHILE CONTINUING WESTWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 200 AM PDT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...20.3N 118.6W
ABOUT 585 MI...945 KM WSW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...85 MPH...140 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...W OR 270 DEGREES AT 8 MPH...13 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...976 MB...28.82 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 200 AM PDT (0900 UTC), the center of Hurricane Rachel was located
near latitude 20.3 North, longitude 118.6 West. Rachel is moving 
toward the west near 8 mph (13 km/h). A westward to 
west-northwestward motion is expected during the next few days.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 85 mph (140 km/h) with higher 
gusts. Gradual weakening is forecast during the next 48 hours. 
 
Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 40 miles (65 km) from the
center and tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 150 miles
(240 km).
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 976 mb (28.82 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF: Swells generated by Rachel will continue to affect the coast
of the Baja California Peninsula and portions of southern California
for the next several days. These swells are likely to cause
life-threatening surf and rip current conditions. Please consult
products from your local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 800 AM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Gibbs
item.author: nhcwebmaster@noaa.gov (NHC Webmaster)

item.title: Hurricane Rachel Forecast Discussion Number 36
item.description:
Issued at 800 PM PDT Mon Oct 05 2026 
877 
WTPZ43 KNHC 060235
TCDEP3
 
Hurricane Rachel Discussion Number  36
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP182026
800 PM PDT Mon Oct 05 2026
 
The visible satellite presentation for Rachel has become far less
impressive than it was earlier today. The eye of the hurricane has
started to fill in again and the deep convection has become
asymmetric based on the infrared imagery. Using a combination of
the objective and subjective intensity estimates, the initial
intensity has been held at 80 kt for this advisory.

The hurricane is moving westward at 8 kt steered by a high pressure
system to the north-northeast of the cyclone. This area of high 
pressure is expected to keep Rachel moving generally westward to 
west-northwestward for the next several days. However, towards the 
end of the week, that high pressure system should weaken as a mid- 
to upper-level trough amplifies near the west coast of the United 
States. As a result, Rachel is expected to slow down and then turn 
northeastward at the end of the forecast period. The current NHC 
forecast track is similar to the previous track, but adjusted based 
on the HCCA and GDMI forecast aids.

The cyclone is expected to move into a region with drier air and 
significantly cooler sea-surface temperatures. Therefore, the 
current NHC intensity forecast has Rachel progressively weakening in 
a similar trend to the previous forecast. The intensity forecast is 
on the upper end of the guidance envelope, but is very close to the 
HCCA forecast aid.
